name: RB2b
tagline: Identifies individual people who visit your B2B website and pushes their profiles into Slack or your CRM.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Plans are credit based on identified visitors, with a free tier.

verdictSummary: The tracking script is trivial: a few lines of JavaScript posting page views to your own endpoint. The product is not the script, it is the identity graph that turns an anonymous hit into a named person with a LinkedIn profile and a work email, US traffic only, built from cookie pools and data partnerships you cannot replicate in an afternoon or legally assemble yourself. You can absolutely self-host first-party analytics and get company-level guesses from IP and ASN lookups, which is a different and much weaker product. Person-level resolution without the graph is not a build problem, it is a data access problem. Build the tracker, rent the identity.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted first-party visitor tracker that logs sessions to SQLite, guesses the company from IP and ASN data, and fires a Slack alert when a visitor hits high-intent pages.
requirements: A server or small VPS to host the collector endpoint
Optional paid IP-to-company API key if you want company names instead of raw ASN strings
whatYouLose: Person-level identification: names, LinkedIn URLs, work emails. Your version stops at maybe-this-company.
The identity cooperative behind the match rate, which is the entire reason anyone pays.
Native pushes into HubSpot, Salesforce, Clay and the rest of the outbound stack.
Someone else owning the consent, opt-out and privacy posture of de-anonymizing strangers.
Match quality that improves as their network grows, versus your static IP lookup table.
moatNotes: The graph is assembled from cookie pools and data partnerships across many sites, so it gets better the more sites run the pixel. That is a network effect wearing a data moat's coat.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the alternative to person-level resolution is not a cheaper tool, it is not knowing. Sales teams pay for the name and the LinkedIn profile, not for the pageview log, and no amount of clean code produces a name out of an IP address. Every self-hosted version bottoms out at company-level guessing, which most teams already get from their analytics tool for free. The pricing is credit based precisely because the value is the lookup, and the lookup is rented.
notes: The pixel is an afternoon; the identity graph is not. The moat is a cooperative of cookie data across thousands of sites plus the legal appetite to resolve it to a named human.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted first-party website visitor tracker with company-level enrichment and Slack alerts. Stack: TypeScript, Hono running on Node, SQLite via better-sqlite3, no framework beyond that. Single repo, no monorepo, no Docker compose sprawl.

Deliver three parts.

1. A tracking snippet, public/track.js, under 2KB unminified. It generates a persistent visitor id in localStorage, a session id in sessionStorage, and POSTs page url, referrer, title, screen size, timezone and time-on-page to /collect. Use navigator.sendBeacon on pagehide. No third party calls from the browser.

2. A collector API. POST /collect validates the payload, resolves the client IP from x-forwarded-for, and writes a pageview row. Enrich the IP once per session: reverse DNS lookup plus an optional call to an IP-to-company API keyed by IPINFO_TOKEN in .env. If no token is set, fall back to reverse DNS hostname and ASN string only, and store enrichment_source so it is obvious how weak the guess is. Cache enrichment by IP in a table for 30 days. Drop known datacenter, VPN and bot traffic using a simple user-agent blocklist and an ASN heuristic.

3. A dashboard at / behind HTTP basic auth from .env. Server-rendered HTML, no client framework. Show sessions grouped by inferred company, then by visitor id, with the page path sequence, first and last seen, and total time. Add a filter for last 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days. Add a scoring rule engine defined in rules.json: a list of path patterns with point values, for example /pricing is 10 points and /careers is minus 5. When a session crosses SCORE_THRESHOLD, POST a message to SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL with the inferred company, the page path sequence and a link to the session in the dashboard. Fire at most once per session.

Explicitly out of scope, and say so in the README: person-level identification. This build cannot and will not resolve a visitor to a named human, a LinkedIn profile or an email address. That requires a third party identity graph. Do not fake it, do not scrape LinkedIn, do not add a placeholder field pretending it exists.

Also include: a /collect rate limiter by IP, a /health endpoint, a DELETE /visitor/:id route plus a documented opt-out cookie so you have something to point at in a privacy policy, a seed script generating fake traffic for local testing, and a README with the snippet install line and a note that IP-based company guessing is wrong often enough that you should treat it as a hint and not a fact. All secrets in .env, .env.example committed, no telemetry, no analytics on the analytics tool.
